A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and retain identifiable methods and experiments despite renaming and reframing. All 11 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v3 are readable, including v3's supplementary material. v1 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original detector comparisons, fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, and component ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original experimental results, while supplementary Section 6 reports additional LLM-size and search-scale analyses.

M1.justification: VED-SR is renamed SymbolicDet, but entity extraction, symbolic features, the regularized fitness objective, evolutionary search, structured prompts, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. The revised diagram and expanded formalization do not establish a new procedural component.

E1.justification: The four benchmark families, main evaluation categories, and sample counts are retained. However, v3 omits concerts from ERA's PersonCrowd description while retaining 352 images. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an editorial omission or an actual change in evaluated event coverage.

E2.justification: The ConvVQ comparator, reported at 90.2 in v1 Table 2, is removed from v3 Table 3; the other UCSD Ped2 comparators remain. EVA-CLIP, DINOv2, and LLAVA already participate in v1's radar comparison, so their explicit citations in v3 do not establish new baselines.

E3.justification: The supplement introduces comparisons across Qwen-7B, 14B, 32B, and 72B, plus a protocol varying the fraction of samples used for symbolic search while evaluating on the remainder. The existing benchmark counts, detection thresholds, and stated 5,000-iteration limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially reworks the supporting analyses: the three ERA-specific with/without-LLM convergence plots are replaced by an LLM-size comparison, and a new sensitivity study examines search-sample allocation on Helmet and Fishing with APE and GLIP. New workplace and sports examples display detections, symbolic rules, and explanations. The manual-logic versus symbolic-regression comparison is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The added curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The supplementary result set adds search-scale findings and replaces the ERA convergence results with Qwen-size curves. The radar also changes reported values: proposed-method illegal fishing decreases from approximately 99.3 to 96.3, cyanobacteria from 99.0 to 96.0, and car-intrusion comparator values increase. ConvVQ's result is removed. Retained main-table scores, including 98.7 on UCSD Ped2, are unchanged; the replacement curves do not establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 adds an overarching search formalization in Equation 3 using LLM guidance, scoring, and detector functions. The regularized symbolic-regression objective, operator space, entity representation, and helmet-counting rule are retained. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the contribution from training-free anomaly-event detection to unlocking complex event understanding in standard object detectors. v3 replaces the explicit approximately 1% annotation claim with a claim of no additional labeled data. Its dataset contribution emphasizes Helmet-Mac's 12,213 samples, which correspond to the already reported training and test counts.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses stochastic search and exponential search-space growth as motivations for LLM guidance. The supplement newly interprets larger search-sample fractions as enabling more accurate and interpretable patterns. Existing explanations concerning semantic guidance, architectural generality, and competitive performance are largely retained.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from eight 32GB V100 GPUs to a 24GB RTX 4090 for detection and Xeon Silver 4214R CPUs for symbolic regression. v3 identifies Qwen models and replaces the GitHub code link with an anonymous SymbolicDet status-page link. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish reruns or actual online resource availability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially replaced: anomaly detection, prompt learning, and open-set detection give way to visual reasoning, neuro-symbolic methods, LLMs for visual tasks, and event understanding. New discussions cite work such as GQA, neural-symbolic VQA, and the neuro-symbolic concept learner, positioning SymbolicDet as modular perception plus explicit reasoning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around an objects-to-events narrative. VED-SR becomes SymbolicDet, the author list changes, and the main-text ablation section is condensed with expanded discussion moved into supplementary Section 6.

P2.justification: The opening training-versus-training-free diagram is removed; the radar is revised and combined with workplace examples. The architecture diagram is redrawn, the fine-tuning and UCSD tables are reordered and reformatted, and the original convergence display is replaced. New search-scale and sports figures appear in the supplement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful sensitivity analyses, LLM and hardware details, and concrete rule examples. However, it replaces dataset-identified ERA convergence plots with an LLM-size plot whose dataset is unspecified, and its abstract incorrectly attributes Table 1's 23.16-point Sport gain to crowd behavior. The added evidence and reduced reporting clarity and consistency leave the net quality direction uncertain.
